title: Validate helper handles and bound response waits
environment: Observed Windows/Tcl helper protocol. This addresses control flow, not all underlying native audio or device failures.
goal: Recover recording/playback UI after helper launch or response failure.
approach: Historical failed assumption: Any nonempty handle string was treated as a channel, and a helper was assumed eventually to answer.
what_worked: Historical correction: Check live-channel membership, convert EOF/read/write/timeout into normal errors, use finite event-driven waits, and clear handles/busy state while releasing helpers on every exit. Verification reported by the source: A stale error string injected before a second stop triggered safe controller recovery; a third recording succeeded. Consecutive cycles passed and termination completed within eight seconds with no residual processes.
what_failed: Historical observed failure: Launch error text remained in a channel-handle variable, causing modal write errors; a wait ignoring EOF/deadline hung stop and left the UI busy.
why: Confirmed: diagnostic text and resource identity shared storage, while protocol waits lacked terminal failure handling.
improved_method: Keep handles distinct from diagnostics. Test helper death between request and response, and make cleanup plus return-to-idle unconditional.
when_to_use: Observed Windows/Tcl helper protocol. This addresses control flow, not all underlying native audio or device failures.
when_not_to_use: This addresses control flow, not all underlying native audio or device failures.
known_limitations: This is an independently curated generalization of an earlier recorded failure. No source-side experiment was rerun during this registration; observation_date is the 2026-10-09 knowledge-review date, not the incident date. Applicability and root-cause claims remain limited to the source-reported conditions.
